Package hadur2.core.model

Class BotOrders

java.lang.Object
hadur2.core.model.BotOrders
public final class BotOrders extends Object
What the robot should do this tick. A field left as NaN means "leave the previous setting in place", as when an AdvancedRobot does not call the setter. A firePower of 0 means do not fire.

The core's answer to one BotInput: HadurCore.tick fills a BotOrders.Builder while it handles the tick, and Guard returns the result, or its own safe orders when the core throws or returns nothing (RES-1). The adapter then calls the matching AdvancedRobot setters: setMaxVelocity, setTurnRightRadians, setAhead, setTurnGunRightRadians, setTurnRadarRightRadians, and setFire only for a positive power, before execute(). Angles are radians, clockwise positive; distances pixels.

equals(java.lang.Object) compares fields with Double.compare(double, double), under which NaN equals NaN, so "no order" matches "no order" when the replay checks that recorded and replayed orders are identical (CORE-2).

From A4 the orders also carry the messages to broadcast to teammates this tick (messages()), each a byte array in the core's link format (LINK-1). Off a team there are none, and the adapter sends nothing.
